Mr Aliyu: Our box-toy school needs a strip to cover its name label. Which
strip will reach?
Aishatu: I built the school. I will wait while we compare.
Adamu: Give everyone a fair turn with the strips.

Start together, then compare
Read together. Use the workbook or an exercise book.
Read together. Keep this textbook reusable.
Mr Aliyu: Length is how far something reaches from one end to
the other. Move the strips so their starts meet. Compare the other
ends. Colour and position do not tell length.
A
B
C
D
B is shortest. C comes next. A is longest of A, B and C. A and D
reach equally far: they have the same length.
Grace: From shortest to longest: B, C, A. I checked the ends.
Mr Aliyu puts his finger flat on paper. He marks its start and tip. He lifts his finger. He draws
a line from the start mark past the tip mark. He puts his finger back: the line reaches
beyond it. His line is longer. Watch your teacher do this before you try.

Repeat one unit carefully
Read together. Use the workbook or an exercise book.
Read together. Keep this textbook reusable.
Mr Aliyu: Open one hand: thumb tip to little-finger tip is a hand span.
Keep that same spread. Mark its end, lift and start there again. Repeat
with no gaps or overlaps. Count full spans.
Watch me measure a reachable table. Say whose spans and how many.
If a part is left, say the full count and a part. Do not call a part a whole
span.
Distance is how far from one place to another. On a clear, safe path,
watch me repeat my usual step heel-to-heel. Keep steps as equal as
possible. Mark the finish. Count my steps; name my unit.
A paper-strip unit works the same way. Each gap below is one copy of
the same strip. A is 3 units; B is 5. The label needs 4. B reaches; A is too
short.
A
B
Label
People have different spans and steps. Their counts alone cannot tell which object is longer.
Use one person and unit for a fair comparison.

Next session: listen and observe
Read together. Use the workbook or an exercise book.
Length / Educational review edition
Adult: delayed recall, before reminders. Use different materials
next session. Swap the positions of a new pair of strips. Ask which is
longer and shorter, and why. Include an equal pair too. Offer three new
different-length pencils to arrange. Ask how the ends helped.
Ask for a new reachable edge measured in the pupil's hand spans and a
safe clear route in that pupil's steps. Record person, unit, full count and
any part. Then offer a different label and strips. Ask the pupil to
compare, order, measure and choose one that fits.
Record observed evidence in the workbook, an exercise book or a
teacher record. Do not supply an invented measurement. If a route or
body-unit action is unavailable, mark it not assessed. A seated
paper-strip route is valid adapted measurement evidence, not evidence
of walking or hand spans.

PRIMARY ONE / TEXTBOOK
LONGER, SHORTER AND FARTHER
Guide, words and next learning
Read together. Use the workbook or an exercise book.
Length / Educational review edition
Prepare: similar safe paper strips, pencils, book, reachable table, fixed
paper-strip unit and label. Adult cuts paper. Clear a short route; supervise
steps. No ruler or centimetres are needed. Read aloud; pointing, speech and
moving objects are valid responses. Place all materials within reach.
Misconceptions and help: If a pupil chooses by position/colour, align starts
and trace to the far ends. If ordering is hard, compare two then add the third.
If units gap or overlap, mark each finish and restart there. Different people's
counts alone do not show longer: use one person's unit. For leftovers record
full units and a part. Recheck with new materials on the try-again page.
Glossary: length: extent end to end; longer/shorter: more/less length; equal length:
same reach with starts aligned; distance: how far between places; hand span:
thumb-tip to little-finger-tip spread; unit: one chosen repeat; step: one repeated
pace; order: arrange by length.
Provisional mapping: historical P1-p09-01 to 05; source Q1-Q6 and S010-S012.
Assumptions P1-A03/A09 apply. Current NERDC alignment and adoption are not
established.
